business_problem: Hundreds of shadow data lakes and tens of thousands of reports created inconsistent metrics, slow benchmarking, and poor governance for Kimberly-Clark's supply-chain and growth initiatives.
solution_summary: Kimberly-Clark collapsed hundreds of decentralized repositories into a single enterprise data lake on Snowflake so supply-chain, R&D, pricing, and marketing teams could work from common governed data. Working with Tredence, the company re-architected its environment in about two years, built a unified ingestion layer, and replaced scattered reporting with a curated KPI library. More than 500 lakes and 30,000 reports were reduced to one Snowflake-centered platform with about 400 KPIs and roughly 2,000 reports that stakeholders use for day-to-day decisions. The data lake now supports cost benchmarking across 18,000 SKUs, supply-chain alerts, revenue-growth analytics, and decades of R&D information in one place, while a natural-language interface lets users ask market-share and business questions without hunting through legacy reports. Snowflake also underpins the company's emerging agentic orchestration layer for end-to-end supply-chain processes.

data_flow: Data from hundreds of shadow lakes and business domains is ingested into Snowflake through a unified ingestion layer. KPI libraries, benchmarking analyses, supply-chain alerts, R&D analytics, and natural-language queries all run against the same governed enterprise lake and feed supply chain, marketing, and product teams.
business_outcome: Kimberly-Clark saved about $1 billion through better visibility into cost of sales, removed tens of thousands of redundant reports, cut ingestion time to value 70%, and saved 30,000 hours on product-cost benchmarking while opening the door to agentic AI.
